 Why Is Alibaba Stock Crashing Before Earnings?
 Harsh Notariya Wed, November 18, 2026 at 11:37 PM PST 2 min read BABA -2.47% 
 Trade BABA on Coinbase Trading disclosure Trading disclosure

 Learn more Photo by BeInCrypto Alibaba stock has lost 16.9% in five sessions, closing Wednesday at $84.37, its lowest finish since January 2025. A new U.S. chip rule, heavy AI spending, and a fading buyback are hitting the shares hours before earnings. 
 Yet the cloud business is growing 45% a year. Shareholders are paying for that growth in cash, and the stock is down 42% in 2026. 
 1. Can Alibaba Still Rent the Chips It Cannot Buy? 
 The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS), the Commerce Department's export-control arm, released an interim final rule on Nov. 16. 
 The rule requires a license to ship advanced chips to data centers that serve China-headquartered companies at scale. 
 Yahoo Finance data show the U.S.-listed shares fell 7% on Nov. 12 as reports of the rule circulated. 
 However, the rule exempts commercial recommender systems, including those run by online retailers. The pressure therefore falls on AI model training. 
 2. Is the AI Buildout Costing More Than It Earns? 
 Alibaba's June-quarter results show capital expenditure rose 75% to RMB67.7 billion ($10 billion). 
 Free cash flow was an outflow of RMB44.7 billion, against RMB18.8 billion a year earlier. 
 Net income fell 75% to RMB10.4 billion. Meanwhile, revenue from China e-commerce, the business funding the buildout, declined 8%. 
 The cloud segment earned RMB5.6 billion in adjusted operating profit. The AI Labs and Applications unit lost RMB13.9 billion. 
 BABA Stock Price Performance. Source: TradingView 3. Who Buys the Dip When Alibaba Does Not? 
 Quarterly repurchases peaked at $5.8 billion in the June 2024 quarter, according to a company update. In the June 2026 quarter, the figure was $162 million. 
 Exchange filings show the last burst of buying in late June and early July, at roughly $97 per American depositary share. The stock now trades 13% below that level. 
 The repurchase program runs through March 2027. It had $19.1 billion unused as of September 2025. 
 What Would Turn Alibaba Stock Around? 
 Results arrive before the U.S. open on Thursday. The chip rule takes effect the same day, on publication in the Federal Register. 
 Three numbers from the June quarter set the bar. 
 Cloud revenue growth, 45% 
 Free cash flow, a RMB44.7 billion outflow 
 Share repurchases, $162 million 
 Beyond the print, data centers serving Chinese customers have 90 days, until mid-February 2027, to obtain a license. 
 If cloud growth holds near 45% and management presents a compute plan built on domestic chips, the bearish read weakens. In contrast, slower growth with another large outflow would suggest the rule is compounding a funding gap. 
 Alibaba's answer could indicate whether China's AI buildout can pay for itself without rented U.S. chips or buyback support.
